This AI is a predator program. These are ones that bank on wording like “YOUR idea/Project” or “start YOUR pitch”… these phrases catch the attention of anyone who says “man, I have a great idea for a _____, but I have no idea how to present it..”. Which to be fair, is most of us everywhere- no matter where we’re scrolling. We’re under assumption that we found an app to be our solution. But it’s our projects first problem and biggest as well.  We get excited enough to hand the entire FRAGILE idea over to some unknown company and software just because it’s an AI. We trust our app stores to vet so we hand it all over and quickly (because e we only have 7 days to see what it can do) plug in all we have and take a deep breath while waiting for what the advertised product has us expecting. Then we got a snag- we don’t have credits to finish  the last 5 slides. You only get 10 of the 15 but you started thinking you only needed 8…? 
They have your whole idea saved and you have a decision. 
A-Pay to upgrade and finish this process at least, you can always cancel later. 
B- close the window and walk away to use Gemini Notebook because it’s free enough to get you started. 
 Waiting for your free credits to reload as we’ve done everywhere else isn’t an option with this one either. 🤯 why they wouldn’t want you coming back with those daily free credits so you’re doing different parts of what you intend, piece by piece, until you are using it so much & so often for so many things .. and it becomes WORTH upgrading. This application seems to forget the level of competition and that users are learning more and more about the options available to us- and what those options can do for us. 
There’s nothing over been able to check out with my free account that makes this platform unique in any other way besides how profit desperate they come across. The way to use it for free or “free ish” is to work for them to refer others and get THOSE PEOPLE to subscribe instead. It doesn’t just leave out and make their products inaccessible to low income users, it’s credit system of points used for different tasks and abilities for additional credits to be purchased “quickly and easily” is laughable. Even if you subscribe- you’ll be paying for more and more credits to do what several other AI apps can do for free, or even over time as your credits refresh. This message brought to you by the poor folks trying to scale.

title: What is your AI era PowerPoint alternative?

text:
Hi HN! Excited to share something my friend and I have been building over many weekends.

I'm a physicist turned software engineer; my buddy went from consulting to tech. We met at a college where the popular path after graduation was consulting or finance (over a decade ago) so we have a lot of friends in the space. We saw firsthand how much of a consultant/analyst's life is spent in PowerPoint: nudging boxes around, putting talking points into a visual format, “beautifying” slides…etc.

There were already AI presentation tools like Claude and Gamma, but the feedback we kept hearing was:

1. They don't handle importing and editing existing PowerPoint decks well.
2. They rely heavily on templates, so decks look repetitive or generic quickly.
3. They're great for web presentations, but less useful if your workflow ends in .pptx, because they're rarely 100% PowerPoint compatible.

Brightdeck is our attempt at an AI presentation maker/editor for people who still live in PowerPoint and need OOXML compatability. You can import a deck, ask it to add slides or make edits, and export back to PowerPoint. It also generates slides without fixed templates. Instead of picking from a few layouts, it constructs each slide directly: text boxes, shapes, images, icons, diagrams, charts etc.

Two technical challenges were much harder than expected, which is why it took us this long to launch.

The first was PowerPoint compatibility, which means digging deep into OOXML. Claude was quite helpful for parts of the spec, though it gets things wrong A LOT and needs verification, so we ended up printing out and reading the ISO manuals. Some parts aren't fully implemented yet: SmartArt in OOXML has near-infinite styling variations that are poorly defined (e.g., a flowchart can have children but the spec doesn’t define how those children are spaced, so you have to reverse engineer it), and right now we convert charts to images when rendering in PowerPoint. This is not ideal, but it preserves fidelity until we add full spec support.

The second was the canvas and multiplayer editing. We wanted realtime collaboration from day one because retrofitting it later is painful. We use a simplified CRDT-like approach for slide state and syncing. It works well for most object-level edits, but realtime text-box editing isn't fully reliable yet when multiple people edit the same text at the same time. In practice people rarely edit the same text box at the same moment, so we accepted that tradeoff.

We debated building a PowerPoint plugin instead of a web app, but ultimately decided against that because we want to have full control over the UI. It also makes it easier to build an MCP server on top, so users can generate decks in ChatGPT and Claude directly.

For the agentic architecture we picked LangGraph — the modularity makes components easier to test. We used Gemini and Qwen for generation.

For this launch, I used Brightdeck to summarize HN sentiment on a top post this week (Fable 5 release): https://app.brightdeck.ai/presentations/019eae69-bbff-739f-a.... I found the deck version quite entertaining. More examples (all one-shot, warts and all so you can see unfiltered what the product can do): https://brightdeck.ai/showcase/.

The results aren't perfect. Some images are less relevant than they should be. But we think the direction is promising, especially for workflows that need an actual .pptx at the end.

You can try it here: https://brightdeck.ai/. There is a generous free tier and no credit card is required. Mobile is supported but editing on mobile is quite limited at this time, so I would suggest using it on a computer.

My friend and I are longtime HN lurkers and have always wanted to do a Show HN together, so this launch is a special one for us.  We'd love feedback, especially from people who've made a lot of decks, or worked with OOXML, collaborative canvases, or AI document generation.

I’m a student building an AI slide designer.

Most slide generators I’ve tried not really good at following instruction because they rely on predefined templates. You describe what you want, but the output still bends toward the template instead of your instructions.

I’m experimenting with a different approach:

- No templates

- The model follows content and design instructions as literally as possible (structure, tone, layout intent)

- Optimized for people who care about precision, or need to generate slides quickly without manual cleanup

This is still an MVP and I would love to hear your honest feedback:

- do you think this feels better than other AI slide generators (like gamma or canva)? if not, can you explain it why?

and I will iterate this MVP until you love it :))
